paras: The search for William Gauch was a manhunt by "citizens" of the county around Hillsboro, North Carolina, in late June 1881 for a Black man accused of raping a 10-year-old girl. The only report found, a Greensboro dispatch in the Chicago Daily Tribune, ended with the search under way and printed it under the headline "WRETCHES WHO SHOULD BE HUNG WHEN CAUGHT."

The dispatch, dated June 24, opened by referring to the lynching of two men for rape "a few days since" in Stokes County and of another two weeks earlier, which it said had not had "the effect looked for by the lynchers."

According to the dispatch, on the morning of June 24 Lizzie Fluch, the 10-year-old daughter of Mrs. Jennie Fluch, was walking to a spring near Hillsboro when she was accosted by William Gauch, whom it called "a negro of bad character." The dispatch charged that Gauch caught the girl when she tried to run and raped her, and that she lay in a precarious condition. Gauch then left the scene (the printed text reads "He at once died," apparently for "fled"), and "Citizens of the county are looking for him."
No report of Gauch's capture, arrest, trial, or of any violence against him was found in the coverage.

The case reached readers through a single Greensboro dispatch printed in Chicago on June 27, which stated the accusation as fact and gave only the accuser's side. Its headline called for hanging, and the Tribune paired the Hillsboro case with a second dispatch about Charles Gilmor, a Black man accused of an attempted assault at Martinsville, whom posses of citizens were also hunting. No North Carolina paper's account of the case was found.

accounts.label: Greensboro dispatch
accounts.gist: Gauch accosted the girl at a spring, caught her when she ran, and raped her; he fled (OCR 'died') and citizens of the county were looking for him.

framing.detail: The Tribune headed the dispatch "WRETCHES WHO SHOULD BE HUNG WHEN CAUGHT" and set it beside recent Stokes County lynchings and a second accusation against a Black man at Martinsville, presenting the accusation as fact.

record_check.dossier: A manhunt for an accused man with no violence, threat, or capture reported; 'other' (manhunt only) fits better than intimidation.
